newsitem.title: CHILE: Bones found where Chilean detention center stood.
newsitem.headline: Bones found where Chilean detention center stood.

text.p: Construction workers erecting a building in downtown Santiago have found the buried remains of five people where a secret police detention centre once stood during General Augusto Pinochet's military rule, Chilean authorities said on Sunday.
Workers discovered the bones on Friday while working on a construction site on Santiago's main avenue, Alameda, authorities told reporters at the site.
The bones appeared to belong to four adults and a child and were found by accident in a vacant lot where a building used as a detention centre by Pinochet's feared DINA secret police used to stand.
The Santiago newspaper El Mercurio said Sunday that forensic experts had determined the bones were less than 20 years old.
If confirmed, that finding would suggest the bodies were buried while the building was used by the DINA and that they may be "disappeared" opponents of Pinochet's rule.
Workers said they also found what looked like the remains of underground cells and passageways at the site, El Mercurio said.
About 2,000 people were kidnapped by state security forces during Pinochet's rule and never seen alive again by their relatives, a state investigative commission said.

Many disappeared at the hands of the now-defunct DINA, whose chief, retired General Manuel Contreras, is currently serving a jail term for planning the 1976 murder of former foreign minister Orlando Letelier in a car bomb in Washington.
